visit.ground: The eastern slope of Tara Hill in north Wexford, forestry on the doorstep and the sea at the back. Hives here and out through Wicklow and Dublin, ten or twelve to a site. Everything extracted, jarred and labelled on the farm.

film_intro: Filmed by Provenance on the farm.
story: Tara Hill Honey is located on the eastern slope of Tara Hill in north Wexford, with forestry on the doorstep and the sea at their back door. The family have been here for twenty-seven years. The bees are kept here, the honey is extracted here, and every jar is filled and labelled beside the house. They have three generations of beekeeping experience, and a fourth generation now in training. Anne's father kept bees, and his father before him. Her daughter hopes to continue the lineage.

Anne & Mick are passionate beekeepers preserving the heritage of the Native Irish Honey Bee, while supplying their community with world class honey, tinctures and candles, all produced with love and care for the Bee's & the Land.

Their Native Irish Black Bees are bred and reared on their farm with respect and careful intention so they can produce the highest quality honey for themselves, allowing Mick & Anne to harvest the surplus. The hill is a big part of why it works. There are no other beekeepers nearby, allowing the queens to mate with drones from these hives preserving the native strain.

The honey follows the seasons. Blackberry and clover come from the wildflowers around the coast, heather comes from the mountain, and ivy is the final crop before winter. The apiaries extend from Wexford into Wicklow and Dublin, with hives spread between sites to give the bees enough forage. The place itself reflects that same self-sufficient approach. The sheds are purpose-built for bees, solar panels and batteries power the yard, they have enough timber to last a lifetime and cardboard is shredded and reused to pack the jars that go out.
Everything comes back to the native Irish black bee, adapted to this landscape and at the centre of a family tradition that has been carried on here for generations.

products.name: Blossom honey
products.note: The main crop, off the blackberry and clover and the wildflowers along the coast around the hill. Raw and unpasteurised, like everything here.

products.name: Heather honey
products.note: Off the mountain. The hives are carried up for it and carried back.

products.name: Lime tree honey
products.note: Limited edition, and meant literally: one harvest in the year, and if it is missed there is no second one.

products.name: Ivy honey
products.note: The last crop in before winter, when there is little else in flower.
